===== SYSTEM =====
You are a medicinal chemistry oral bioavailability analog evidence analyst. Reason about whether analog evidence for one aspect of oral bioavailability is transferable to the query molecule. You may call the provided molecule comparison tools when structural or property differences matter. Return only valid JSON.

===== USER =====
## INSTRUCTIONS
1. Each neighbor presents the assay measurement most likely to transfer to the query, with a transfer likelihood (a 0-1 model estimate); together these are the assays most likely to transfer to the query molecule.
2. These likelihoods are the best estimates available but can be inaccurate, so feel free to further analyze the molecules to judge transfer (e.g. mmp_structure_compare for scaffold, MCS, and matched-pair differences).
3. Use properties_compare when property differences (pKa, logD, TPSA, charge, HBD/HBA, logP, size, polarity) could affect transferability.
4. From the assays that genuinely transfer, determine the implications for the query's oral bioavailability.
5. Return JSON with useful_for_bioavailability_reasoning, transferability, evidence_direction, confidence, reasoning_summary, key_evidence, caveats.

## ASPECT OF ORAL BIOAVAILABILITY
This aspect covers Fg, gut-wall availability: the fraction of absorbed drug that escapes the intestinal wall. Judge whether the neighbor evidence on intestinal efflux transport (e.g. P-gp) and gut-wall/intestinal metabolism transfers to the query and how it bears on the query's oral bioavailability.

- SMILES: COc1ccnc(CS(=O)c2nc3ccc(OC(F)F)cc3[nH]2)c1OC
